title: Human-AI Collaboration in Biomedicine
audience: Clinical learners reflecting on human-AI collaboration tools in care settings
objectives: Identify human-AI collaboration tools currently used in clinical practice.
Evaluate benefits, drawbacks, governance, and data-management practices for those tools.
Analyze possible hospital responses to AI transcription errors in patient-care settings.
Practice balancing documentation efficiency against patient safety, fairness, trust, and privacy risks.

sections.name: Question 1
sections.purpose: Inventory current human-AI collaboration tools in clinical work.
sections.how_to_use: List tools used in clinical practice, explain how they are used, note benefits and drawbacks, and describe how outputs/data are managed.

sections.name: Question 2
sections.purpose: Analyze a flawed AI transcription system in hospital care.
sections.how_to_use: Consider hallucinated content, inaccurate tone, accent-related errors, documentation risk, patient safety, and what the hospital should do next.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through Question 1 first, then the clinical transcription case.
For clinical users, emphasize patient safety, chart integrity, clinician oversight, accent bias, privacy, and workflow governance.
Help learners propose concrete routes such as pause deployment, audit, vendor remediation, human review, consent updates, or limited monitored use.
